title: Mitigating Data Imbalance in Time Series Classification Based on Counterfactual Minority Samples Augmentation

problem.claim: Imbalanced time-series classification is a critical and challenging task across real-world applications.

gap.claim: Existing oversampling and generative approaches may overlook causal factors and fail to improve class separability, especially with ambiguous class boundaries.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes the CounterFactual Augmentation Minority Generation method, which uses generative models to discover class-determining causal factors.

The method separates causal and non-causal factors with a disentangled classifier and performs counterfactual intervention by replacing majority-sample causal factors with minority-sample causal factors.
A minority-class decoder generates counterfactual minority samples intended to retain essential structures while remaining distinguishable from the original majority class.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments outperform state-of-the-art methods on univariate and multivariate imbalanced time-series classification tasks.
The authors report that the code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Imbalanced time-series classification is important but difficult.
Prior methods focus on minority classes and may rely on static boundaries or similarity heuristics, while overlooking causal factors and class-boundary ambiguity.
CFAMG identifies causal and non-causal factors, intervenes on latent representations, and decodes counterfactual minority samples.
The authors report superior performance across univariate and multivariate tasks and provide code.

source_observation.claim: The described augmentation procedure intervenes on class-related latent factors while preserving essential structures.

interpretation.claim: For imbalanced sequence data, separating class-relevant factors from other factors may provide a basis for more targeted synthetic examples.

application.claim: A related application could test causal-factor-guided augmentation when minority samples are scarce and class boundaries are ambiguous.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the assumed causal and non-causal factors are identifiable or reliable across domains.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not detail the generative architecture, training procedure, or causal assumptions.
